The only line added is '; CHECK-NEXT:   # implicit-def: $f{{[0-9]+}}_d' at llvm/test/CodeGen/RISCV/freploop-nested.ll:60, between main1's 'CHECK: li [[rBound]], 127' (line 59) and 'CHECK-NEXT: frep.o [[rBound]], 2, 0, 0' (line 61). evidence.four_run_lines: I ran build/20-T008/bin/llc myself (built 11:53, after the T003 source change at 11:43; RISCVInstrInfo.cpp:3259-3260 has the FREP_O/FREP_I cases) with default, -O1, -O2 and -O3 -mcpu=snitch -snitch-frep-inference. evidence.oracle_still_bites: With build/int-20/bin/llc (no T003) the edited test FAILS at all four levels. The first failure is in main at line 15 (fmul.d hoisted above li/frep.o). To show that main1's edited block catches the miscompile on its own, I checked main1's output alone (sed from 'main1:') against the test's check lines 50+. It FAILS at all four levels with int-20 and PASSES at all four with 20-T008. With int-20, main1 emits 'fmul.d' then '# implicit-def: $f14_d' then 'li' then 'frep.o' then 'fadd.d', so frep.o would repeat the wrong two instructions, and the strict chain rejects it.

That is correct: the added line matches an assembler comment for an IMPLICIT_DEF pseudo, the instructions checked are unchanged, and the frep count is 3/3. The report explains why update_llc_test_checks.py was not used: the test is a hand-written fork test, and the owner exception covers this one-line hand edit. No semantic rows.
